rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice when something is extremely difficult.

example.english: This maths problem is fiendish; I’ve thought about it all morning and still can’t solve it.
example.traditional: 呢條數學題好難，我諗咗成朝都未識做。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 sou3 hok6 tai4 hou2 naan4 ngo5 nam2 zo2 sing4 ciu4 dou1 mei6 sik1 zou6

rows.note: Use this for the general sense of being evil or fiend-like.

example.english: The fiendish wizard in the story is always trying to hurt people.
example.traditional: 故仔入面嗰個邪惡巫師成日想害人。
example.jyutping: gu2 zai2 jap6 min6 go2 go3 ce4 ok3 mou4 si1 seng4 jat6 soeng2 hoi6 jan4

rows.note: Use this instead of 邪惡 when the sinister quality involves deceit, underhandedness, or a hidden threat.

example.english: They seem to help you, but secretly undermine you—they’re fiendish.
example.traditional: 佢表面話幫你，背後卻搞小動作，真係好陰險。
example.jyutping: keoi5 biu2 min6 waa6 bong1 nei5 bui3 hau6 koek3 gaau2 siu2 dung6 zok3 zan1 hai6 hou2 jam1 him2
